ui: Allow dismissing debug output with Esc, fix detachable issues The new debug output using the HWID font looks pretty, but it does bring a few new UX issues since it often completely overlays the main firmware screen. This patch adds the ability to force redrawing the screen (i.e. dismissing any debug text that might be on there) by pressing Esc (which is probably the most natural thing a user would press to try to get rid of the text). This check for Esc happens after any other key checks, so pressing it at the TO_DEV screen will still return you to the recovery screen (as it has before). I also noticed some problems when dismissing debug info by selecting a different menu option in the detachable UI: we don't normally redraw the whole screen when switching between options, so this will still leave the debug output in the background (which is usable but ugly). With this patch the detachable UI will always redraw the screen on the first draw request after displaying debug info. BRANCH=None BUG=None TEST=Manually went through affected transitions on Kevin (both clamshell and detachable). Change-Id: Ifadbc1a258bb7a7f8029e0f1f1786230aa724ae5 Signed-off-by: Julius Werner <jwerner@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1548301 Reviewed-by: Furquan Shaikh <furquan@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Shelley Chen <shchen@chromium.org>

pytest: Don't pickle the python exception. CL:1477132 tried to provide a more structured way to report the raised exception from pytests to goofy. The approach pickles exceptions so that they can be send to the event queue and saved to files. However, most of the exception can't be pickled (see https://bugs.python.org/issue27015 for more detail). This CL revises the related modules to prevent the exception instances from being serialized. `cros.factory.test.test_case.TestCase` now stores the exception instance locally instead of posting it to the event queue directly. `cros.factory.test.pytest_runner` dumps the exception message and its traceback list instead of the whole instance to the output file. BUG=chromium:933275 TEST=make test; manual test Change-Id: I03a6fecf712c01839d2b4bb36d99ca50684ded79 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1545340 Commit-Ready: Yong Hong <yhong@google.com> Tested-by: Yong Hong <yhong@google.com> Reviewed-by: Wei-Han Chen <stimim@chromium.org>

power: suspend_stress_test: const factor optimization for memory test Since the refactor of RTC wakealarm moves the RTC programming to the setuid helper, the data meaning of the suspend time parameter would be suspend period rather than a budget time, therefore we are now safe to remove the workarounds for the demanding memory test. Such that, it not only simplifies the test script but also gives a const factor optimization. i.e., A Yorp N4100 8GiB SKU could take 74m41.774s in 100 iterations, while applying the patch it would reduce the time to 67m41.921s; Think about the scaling, it would save lots of time on partners' engineering when it comes to the validation of a new memory part. Notice the time varies by CPU computation power (memory fill) and the total size of DRAM (presuming do memory check as much as possible) BUG=chromium:941846, b:73018133 TEST=do 'time suspend_stress_test -c 100 --memory_check' to benchmark the consumed time. crash: Don't allow system crashes to starve uploading of user crashes Sort crashes by timestamp across all crash directories; upload the oldest first. This avoids cases where, if something is writing crash reports to /var/spool/crash constantly, it prevents any user crashes from being uploaded. Also minor refactoring: I added a move constructor to brillo::KeyValueStore in https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromiumos/platform2/+/1532844, so now I can change MetaFile from holding a unique_ptr to a CrashInfo to just holding a CrashInfo. Faster, less deferencing, and no need to worry about the pointer being NULL. BUG=chromium:326584 TEST=Unit tests, plus ran a script that generated selinux_violation files in /var/spool/crash every 10 seconds. Confirmed that crashes in user directory still got uploaded eventually. Change-Id: I3017566092493d6ae5f8ab38de9f3d319d7219c0 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1548417 Commit-Ready: Ian Barkley-Yeung <iby@chromium.org> Tested-by: Ian Barkley-Yeung <iby@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Jeffrey Kardatzke <jkardatzke@google.com>
